claim: Conductor advances workflow executions by evaluating discrete task states against JSON DAG specifications (WorkflowDef), scheduling subsequent tasks via DeciderService without worker coroutine replay.
mechanism: DeciderService.decide(workflow) inspects current task states in WorkflowModel. Executable downstream tasks are mapped using specialized TaskMappers and emitted in DeciderOutcome for queue dispatch and DAO persistence.
applicabilityConditions: Workflows composed of SIMPLE, FORK_JOIN, DECISION/SWITCH, DO_WHILE, and SUB_WORKFLOW tasks
localContext: DeciderService.decide(workflow) inspects current task states in WorkflowModel. Executable downstream tasks are mapped using specialized TaskMappers and emitted in DeciderOutcome for queue dispatch and DAO persistence. Known limits: Workflows must be expressible as predefined JSON DAG structures; dynamic imperative code branching is limited to script/switch task evaluations.

claim: Workflow progression and timeout enforcement do not rely solely on real-time worker callbacks; a background reconciliation sweeper (WorkflowSweeper) periodically re-evaluates active workflows from delayed queues.
mechanism: When a workflow or task is scheduled, its ID is pushed to deciderQueue with a delay offset. WorkflowSweeper polls the queue, acquires the execution lock, checks task timeouts and unacknowledged leases, repairs missing queue messages via WorkflowRepairService, and triggers decide().
applicabilityConditions: All active running workflows in Conductor clusters
localContext: When a workflow or task is scheduled, its ID is pushed to deciderQueue with a delay offset. Known limits: Sweeper introduces a polling interval delay for timeout detection (typically 30-60s) unless short sweep intervals are configured.

claim: Task distribution is mediated by queue abstractions (QueueDAO) with unacknowledged visibility timeout leases, ensuring task redelivery if workers crash before completing.
mechanism: WorkflowExecutor pushes task IDs to QueueDAO. Workers poll for tasks and receive a temporary unack timeout lease. If the worker completes, updateTask removes the task; if the worker crashes, the queue unack timeout expires, re-exposing the task for subsequent worker polling.

Known limits: Workers must be idempotent because unack timeout expirations during long-running tasks can cause concurrent duplicate execution by another worker.

claim: Concurrent evaluation triggers for the same workflow instance (from parallel task completions, external events, or sweeper ticks) are serialized using distributed execution locks.
mechanism: WorkflowExecutor.decide acquires an execution lock on workflowId via ExecutionLockService (backed by RedisLock, ZookeeperLock, or LocalOnlyLock). The lock is reentrant and auto-released after evaluation completion or lease expiry.
applicabilityConditions: All decide() evaluations across multi-node Conductor clusters

claim: Operational workflow and task state is isolated in high-throughput transactional/KV storage, while audit history and search queries are decoupled via ExecutionDAOFacade to Elasticsearch.
mechanism: ExecutionDAOFacade writes primary workflow and task models synchronously to ExecutionDAO (Redis, Cassandra, Postgres, MySQL) and asynchronously enqueues search index updates to IndexDAO (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch).
applicabilityConditions: All workflow creation, update, and search operations
localContext: ExecutionDAOFacade writes primary workflow and task models synchronously to ExecutionDAO (Redis, Cassandra, Postgres, MySQL) and asynchronously enqueues search index updates to IndexDAO (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch). mechanism: ExecutionDAOFacade checks payload size against maxPayloadSize. Large payloads are uploaded via ExternalPayloadStorage (S3, GCS, Azure) and replaced with an externalStoragePath URI in the database model. TaskModel preserves active in-memory outputData during iterative evaluations.
